Carry out the test for protein on different concentrations of milk using step 1 to step 9.
The syringe labelled M must be used only for the 100% M.
1. Prepare the concentrations of milk as decided in (a)(i) and as shown in Fig. 1.1.
Use a glass rod to mix the milk solution and water.
2. Label the test-tubes with the concentrations of milk as prepared in step 1.
3. Put 1 cm of each concentration into the appropriately labelled test-tube.
4. Label another test-tube 0.0% and put 1 cm of W into this test-tube.
5. Put 1 cm of P into each test-tube. Shake gently tomix.
6. Put 1 cm of C into each test-tube. Shake gently tomix.
7. Leave the test-tubes for at least 2 minutes. Shake gently to mix.
Fig. 1.2 shows the key you need to use to record your results.
A blue colour indicates that the concentration of protein is too low to be detected.

You now need to:
• carry out the test for protein on X using step 10 to step 12
• use your results in (a)(ii) to estimate the concentration of protein in X.
10. Label a test-tube with the letter X.
11. Put 1 cm of X into the test-tube labelled X.
12. Repeat step 5 to step 7, with X.
